The revolution that overthrew the Qing dynasty and ended more than two thousand years of imperial rule in China, from the Qin unification onward. It began with an army uprising at Wuchang on 10 October 1911 and ended with the abdication of the child emperor Puyi in February 1912.

The Qing had lost authority through defeats abroad, the Boxer Rebellion and reforms that came too late. Many educated Chinese resented rule by the Manchus. Revolutionary groups, above all Sun Yat-sen's Revolutionary Alliance, had staged uprisings for years.

When soldiers mutinied at Wuchang, province after province declared independence. Sun returned from abroad and was named provisional president of the Republic of China in Nanjing on 1 January 1912. The court turned to the general Yuan Shikai, who instead arranged the emperor's abdication and took the presidency himself.

The revolution created the Republic of China, but not a stable democracy. After Yuan died in 1916, the country split among warlords. 10 October is still National Day in Taiwan.
